chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Kufi, who is al-'Asimi, from Abd al-Wahid ibn al-Sawwaf, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Hamdani, from Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) used to counsel his companions and say: 'I enjoin upon you taqwa of God, for it is the joy of the hopeful seeker and the refuge of the fleeing one who seeks shelter. Internalize taqwa as your innermost garment, and remember God with a sincere remembrance — you shall live by it the finest of lives and walk by it the path of salvation.

Look at the world with the gaze of the ascetic who has parted from it, for it uproots the settled dweller and brings grief to the affluent who feels secure. Do not hope for what has turned away from it and departed, nor is what is yet to come from it known so that it may be awaited. Affliction from it is joined with ease, and what remains of it ends in extinction. So its joy is tainted with sorrow, and remaining in it leads to weakness and frailty.

It is like a garden whose pasture is lush, amazing those who look upon it — its water is sweet, its soil is good, its roots pour out moisture from the earth, and its branches drip with dew — until the grass reaches its prime and its shoots stand erect, then a wind arises that strips the leaves and scatters what was orderly,
so it becomes — as God said — 'dry broken stubble that the winds scatter, and God is the Holder of power over all things.' (Quran 18:45)
Look at this world — at the abundance of what amazes you, and the scarcity of what benefits you.'

key_terms.البلاء بالرخاء: Affliction connected with ease — the inseparability of hardship and comfort in worldly life
key_terms.الزاهد: Zahid — the ascetic, one who practices zuhd (renunciation of worldly attachments)
key_terms.تقوى الله: God-consciousness, piety, mindfulness of God — the central virtue in Islamic ethics, here presented as both joy and refuge
key_terms.شعاراً باطناً: Inner garment/emblem — metaphor for taqwa being the most intimate aspect of one's spiritual dress
key_terms.هشيماً: Hashim (dry stubble) — Quranic imagery for the perishing of worldly splendor

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about taqwa and the nature of the world (dunya)?
ai.summary: This hadith records Imam al-Kadhim (AS) transmitting an extended sermon attributed to Imam Ali (AS), the Commander of the Faithful, who regularly counseled his companions on taqwa, sincere remembrance of God, and renunciation of worldly attachment (zuhd). Imam Ali draws on vivid botanical imagery — comparing the dunya to a lush garden that is ultimately destroyed by a wind — culminating in a direct citation from Quran 18:45. The audience of early Shia companions would have understood this as a fundamental call to detach from worldly illusions and anchor themselves in God-consciousness. The contrast between what 'amazes' (dazzling appearances) and what 'benefits' (lasting spiritual gain) encapsulates the central message.
word_analysis: I counsel you/I enjoin upon you
so that it may be awaited

en.hubeali: H 14451 – Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Ahmad All Kufy, and he is Al-A’asmiy, from Abdul Wahid Bin Al-Sawwaf, from Muhammad Bin Ismail Al-Hamdany who has narrated the following: Abu Al-Hassan Musaasws having said: ‘Amir-ul-Momineenasws used to bequeath to hisasws companions saying: ‘Iasws bequeath you to fear Allahazwj for it is happiness for the truthful seeker, and a heavy shackle for the runaway fugitive. And be aware of the piety realising it within yourselves, and remember Allahazwj with a sincere Remembrance, being revived by it, and journey upon the path of salvation.

Look at this world with the vision of the ascetics, the ones who have parted from it, for it dislodges its residents and causes distress to the affluent ones who (superficially) feel safe. Do not hope for those that are turned away from it, not knowing what it is that will come from it. So await patiently for the prosperity upon the arrival of the afflictions from it, and the survival from it up to the end.  
So its happiness is tainted with the grief, and the survival in it is up to the weakness and the fragility.

So it is like a garden, the pasture of which is dense causing those who look at it, to wonder at it. Its drinks are sweet, its covering (soil) is good, its roots are excited in the ground, and its branches drip moisture until the grass reaches its due level. The scent gets triggered under the blades and gets separated from it in the morning, just as Allahazwj has Said: “[18:45] then it becomes dry broken into pieces which the winds scatter; and Allah is the holder of power over all things.”
Look at this world and the numerous things which cause you to wonder, and the scarcity of the things which benefit you’.
